conviction_note: This is UNFI's fiscal-year-end print and the first FY27 guide, and it is being delivered by a CFO who started roughly five weeks earlier while his predecessor - the man the shareholder base credits with the entire margin story - moved sideways to COO; the tape shows two high-volume no-news down legs into it, so I take about a third of the 10.18% median to the downside.

findings.finding: UNFI changed CFO five weeks before its fiscal-year-end print: an 8-K carrying items 5.02, 7.01 and 9.01 was accepted 2026-07-09T11:01:43Z, the transition took effect on 2026-08-03 with President and CFO Matteo Tarditi moving to COO and a new CFO starting the following week, and a Form 3 initial statement of beneficial ownership was accepted 2026-08-13T20:18:01Z - so the person who will set the initial FY27 guidance, against a publicly referenced FY27 objective of $800m adjusted EBITDA versus an FY26 guide of $685-705m, has been in the seat for about a month.

findings.why_not_priced: The appointment itself was announced on 9 July and is old news; what is not priced is that this particular print is the one where a new CFO owns the numbers. UNFI's whole equity story in this corpus is margin, not revenue - the shareholder base writes 'EBITDA margin growing from 1.25% to 2.25%, thanks to CFO Matteo Tarditi' and 'margin growth is strong and WAY more important to UNFI than a slight dip in revenue' - and the outgoing CFO was still fronting investor events as recently as the UBS conference on 2026-03-12. A successor's first act on a multi-year margin walk-up is normally to widen or lower the opening bar. If the market had connected the handover to the FY27 guide, the sell side would have marked its targets down rather than raising them across the board after the June print (BMO $56 from $52, UBS $47 from $44, Goldman $47 from $42, Roth $43 from $38, Wells Fargo $56, all on 2026-06-11).
findings.independence: The tape corroborates from a different file: quote.json shows the stock fell from $50.83 on 2026-07-31 to $47.37 on 2026-08-03, -6.8% on 935,700 shares against a 526,595 20-day average, on the exact day the transition took effect - and the shareholder record for that day asks 'has anyone seen news that might explain today's 7% drop when other grocery stocks were flat to slightly up? The only thing I can find is that Matteo Tardini transitioned from CFO to COO today'. So the market did react to the handover once, without a catalyst, which is evidence the handover carries information it has not finished pricing.

findings.finding: Volume built on falling prices in the fortnight before the print with no identifiable news: $48.54 on 08/24 to $43.93 on 09/04, -9.5%, with volume rising through 967,500 on 08/31, 803,600 on 09/03 and 1,095,400 on 09/04 - the last being 2.1x the 526,595 20-day average and the heaviest session in the run-in - while the only shareholder commentary in the window reads 'August ended as it began: selling hard on no news' (2026-08-31); with roughly 61m shares out, institutional ownership reported above 100% of float and short interest of about 2.46m shares or 4.1% of float at 5.2 days to cover, that supply is long liquidation rather than shorts pressing.

findings.why_not_priced: The price is priced; the composition of the selling is not. A screen sees -4.08% over five days and -6.65% over twenty and reads a modest pre-earnings drift. What is actually there is a two-legged, high-volume distribution with no news on either leg, into the fiscal-year-end print of a name whose float is almost entirely institutional and barely shorted - so there is no covering bid waiting underneath and no short base to squeeze on a beat. If shorts were driving it, the 4.1% short-of-float figure would be higher and the days-to-cover longer.
findings.independence: Separate primary source from finding 1 (quote.json versus the filings index), though both lean on the same StockTwits digest for corroboration, so the digest should be collapsed to a single source across the two. The one thing cutting against me: the same digest records a shareholder base that has bought every one of these dips ('this is the 3rd quarter in a row that the market reacted this way to UNFI earnings and buying the dip is 2 for 2 so far', 2026-06-09), and three of the last four reactions were negative, so the fade may already be the consensus trade.

baseline_tension: It agrees with the run-in and with the reaction history, which is the uncomfortable part: three of the last four reactions were negative (-10.28%, -2.99%, +4.63%, +18.45%), the run-in is -4.08% and -6.65%, and the stock is 20.9% off its high - so I am adding to a consensus rather than opposing one, which is why I took a third of the median instead of the whole of it.
